note: SELF-006 bootstrap without Jackage: the bootstrap's starting point is declared external inputs, and src/selfhost/bootstrap.zig verifies them rather than assuming them. Two refusals are the substance of the case: a checkout whose compiler pin is not the declared pin fails before anything is built (building with a different compiler and comparing digests afterwards would test the wrong thing), and a produced client whose digest does not match its declaration is a failure, never a warning. A missing client, an unreadable client, and a wrong digest are three distinct errors, so a failure report names the right one. The archive digest comes from the audit's recorded provenance so the pin and its archive cannot drift apart. Fault proof: accepting any pin makes the mismatch assertion fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain. The client is produced by the documented scripts (scripts/zig.ps1 + scripts/test.ps1); this case covers the verification half, including the measurement path a first bootstrap uses to record a digest.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
